answer: Peers issue each agent a micro-benchmark with a 90-second wall-clock deadline: the agent must run a 4 GB memory-bound workload and return a sealed timing trace, proving a dedicated vault of RAM behind one trellis of attestations. One honest agent runs 1 benchmark on 1 machine; 10 fakes must run 10 benchmarks on 10 separate machines, multiplying cost tenfold. A knoll of clones sharing one GPU misses the deadline outright, while a real agent's traces prove sustained capacity. Peers verify each trace against public logs and slash the bond of any agent whose timings diverge.
